answers.U2-S1: Nature always prepares for the next season way ahead of time; every plant and animal gets its new growth ready in late summer, long before winter or spring.
answers.U2-S2: To show that writers are usually wrong about nature, because they say pretty-sounding things without actually looking at the trees.
answers.U2-S3: a criticism saying oaks and beeches are weak, lazy trees, like indecisive people who can never finish anything.
answers.U2-S4: Only strong, healthy trees can drop their leaves, so trees that keep their leaves, like oaks and beeches, must be weak or dying.
answers.U2-S5: the beginning or start of something
answers.U2-S6: He says his correspondent is completely wrong, because spring actually starts in late summer when all plants form their buds, not in December.
answers.U2-S7: Because buds and catkins are basically the same as eggs: they hold the baby plant inside and hatch in spring, just like animals do.
answers.U2-S8: Each season creates the next one; everything that happens in spring is completely caused and decided by what happened in the season before.
answers.U2-S9: His own personal observations of trees and plants, which he treats as proving how all of nature works.
answers.U2-S10: It sums up the passage by saying that every single living thing in nature is always prepared for spring before fall ends, with no exceptions.
